leaks.note: Illustrative layout, not a client site.
leaks.lede: A WordPress site is only as good as the hands that keep it. Each stage below is where builds go wrong, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Building pages one by one with no template plan.
stages.why: Without planned templates, every new page becomes custom work and the site drifts.
stages.does: We map pages, templates, editing needs and integrations, then agree the scope in writing.

stages.breaks: A bought theme patched with plugins.
stages.why: Every extra plugin adds weight, update work and risk.
stages.does: Approved designs become a custom theme, with plugins kept to the few that earn their place.

stages.breaks: Going live without testing speed, forms and tracking.
stages.why: Slow pages and silent forms lose enquiries before anyone notices.
stages.does: We test speed, forms, tracking and mobile before the switch, then migrate and redirect carefully.

stages.breaks: A site only the builder can edit.
stages.why: If every change needs a developer, pages go stale.
stages.does: Your team gets an editing guide, and we can stay on under website maintenance.

process.note: Timing depends on scope. We agree it with you before work starts.

leaks.note: Illustrative layout, not a client site.
leaks.lede: A site that is cared for keeps earning its place. Each stage below is where care slips, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Updating a site nobody has audited.
stages.why: Old plugins, weak hosting and missing backups stay hidden until something breaks.
stages.does: We check versions, plugins, hosting, backups, security and speed, and list what needs fixing first.

stages.breaks: Updates run straight on the live site.
stages.why: One bad update can break a layout or a form.
stages.does: We set up backups and monitoring, and a safe copy to test updates before they go live.

stages.why: Scans, checks and small edits slip when nobody owns them.
stages.does: Updates, scans, checks and small edits happen on a schedule you can see.

stages.breaks: No record of what was done.
stages.why: Without a summary you cannot tell what was fixed or what comes next.
stages.does: Each month you get a summary, and we suggest changes worth making next.

process.note: Timing depends on scope. We agree it with you before work starts.
